System description:
# Case: Tesla Model X with Autopilot (Mountain View, California, 2018)

Source: NTSB Highway Accident Report HAR-20/01. This is a description of the system and its use before the crash. It does not include the investigation findings.

## System
A 2017 Tesla Model X has Autopilot, a SAE Level 2 partial driving automation feature. It combines Traffic-Aware Cruise Control (TACC) and Autosteer (lane keeping). The driver stays responsible for driving and monitoring the road.

## Main parts
- Sensors: a forward-facing camera, a forward-facing radar and ultrasonic sensors.
- Vision processing: a camera-based system detects lane markings, vehicles and some objects ahead.
- TACC: holds a speed set by the driver, follows a vehicle ahead at a chosen gap, and returns to the set speed when no vehicle is ahead.
- Autosteer: keeps the vehicle in its lane using lane markings and the path of the vehicle ahead.
- Forward collision warning and automatic emergency braking are available as separate features.
- Driver monitoring: steering torque is used to check that the driver's hands are on the wheel, with visual and audible alerts if no hands are detected for a period of time.

## People
- The driver sets the cruising speed, turns Autopilot on, and is told to keep hands on the wheel and watch the road.
- Other road users and road workers share the highway. Road agencies maintain road markings and safety hardware such as barriers and crash attenuators.

## Operating context
Busy multi-lane freeway with high-occupancy-vehicle (HOV) lanes, exits and interchanges, lane markings of different quality, and traffic that changes in speed.

requirements.text: The system shall monitor whether the driver's gaze is directed toward the roadway and, if it is not directed toward the roadway for more than 3 seconds while Autopilot is engaged, issue an audible and visual warning and initiate a safe reduction of assistance if the driver does not respond.

Before enabling Autopilot, the system shall display that the driver remains responsible for driving and must actively supervise, require the driver to acknowledge this message, and repeat the message during operation at least once every 10 minutes.

When the vision system detects a possible relevant hazard but cannot classify or track it with sufficient confidence, the system shall treat the area as potentially occupied, warn the driver, and avoid steering or accelerating in a way that increases collision risk.

If lane-marking or lead-vehicle-path confidence falls below the validated threshold, or those inputs conflict, Autosteer shall not use them as reliable lane guidance; it shall alert the driver and disengage or limit steering before leaving the currently verified safe lane.
When sensor data indicates an imminent collision, the system shall command automatic emergency braking if braking can reduce collision severity, even when the object's classification is uncertain.

When a pedestrian, worker, or other road user is detected in or entering the vehicle's path, the system shall warn the driver and apply braking when needed to reduce collision risk, regardless of whether the road user's presence is expected.

When another vehicle cuts into the gap ahead, TACC shall detect the reduced headway and promptly reduce speed or brake as needed to restore a safe following distance, without exceeding the system's validated response limits.

The system shall not use steering torque alone as evidence that the driver is attentive; while Autopilot is engaged, it shall assess driver attention independently of wheel torque and warn or limit assistance when attention is not confirmed.

The system shall diagnose obstruction, degradation, or unavailability of each forward-facing sensor and, when required forward information is unavailable, alert the driver and disable or limit the affected assistance functions until sensor availability is restored.

When TACC loses or drops its tracked lead vehicle, it shall not resume the set speed until the forward path has been independently confirmed clear for at least 2 seconds; if the path cannot be confirmed, it shall maintain or reduce speed and alert the driver.
